_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory AML with a susceptible NPM1 mutation who have no satisfactory alternative treatment options

pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with relapsed or refractory AML with an NPM1 mutation (Type A, B, D and other mutations likely to result in cytoplasmic localization of NPM1 protein)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Rate of complete remission (CR) plus CR with partial hematological recovery (CRh)
pivotal_trials.n: N=112 (pooled Phase 1b and Phase 2 patients treated at 600 mg once daily)
pivotal_trials.result: CR+CRh in 24 (21.4%) patients (95% CI 14.2, 30.2); median duration of CR+CRh 5.0 months (95% CI 1.9, 8.1); CR 19 (17.0%)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) include infection without an identified pathogen (52%), hemorrhage (38%), diarrhea (36%), nausea (35%), fatigue (34%), edema (30%), bacterial infection (28%). Serious adverse reactions in 79% of patients; fatal adverse reactions in 4 (4%). Boxed warning for differentiation syndrome; QTc interval prolongation in 12%.
target_moa: Ziftomenib is a menin inhibitor that blocks the interaction between menin and KMT2A, disrupting leukemogenic transcriptional signaling

boxed_warning.content: Differentiation syndrome, which can be fatal, has occurred with KOMZIFTI; if suspected, interrupt KOMZIFTI and initiate corticosteroids

companion_dx_detail: No FDA-approved test for the detection of NPM1 mutations is currently available; a companion diagnostic study is a post-marketing commitment

summary.text: KOMZIFTI (ziftomenib) received traditional approval for R/R AML with a susceptible NPM1 mutation, supported by Study KO-MEN-001 (21.4% CR+CRh rate). The program had Orphan drug (2019), Fast Track (2023), and Breakthrough Therapy (2024) designations, and the NDA was reviewed under Priority review.
